newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mostly lower.

text.p: Bids for dark northern spring wheat were mostly lower on Wednesday and movement was slow as farmers prepared for harvest, several cash grain dealers said.

"If the weather holds they'll start into the fields in the next week or so," a Montana dealer said. "People were kind of concerned about the protein being a little low but now I think we'll fall just about normal."

But further east, harvest was still at least two weeks away and quality was of increasing concern. A tour of North Dakota spring wheat found scab infestation in the eastern part of the state and moisture stress in the south.

Participants on one leg of the Wheat Quality Council tour said an early summer drought and disease caused significant reduction in the wheat's yield potential. The tour on Tuesday calculated an average spring wheat yield potential for the first day of 31.1 bushels per acre.
